title: Dispute Escrow for Agent Payments on Pix/UPI
angle: AI agents & the agent economy x Emerging markets leapfrogging
one_liner: A neutral hold-and-evidence layer that gives agent-initiated Pix and UPI payments the dispute protection cards have and push rails never did.
customer: Brazilian WhatsApp-commerce, bill-pay and shopping-agent startups and their sponsoring payment institutions, plus Indian UPI apps building agentic checkout. Marketplaces and merchants who want to accept agent buyers are the second payer.
problem: Pix, UPI and M-Pesa are push rails: instantly final, with no chargeback culture. When an agent buys the wrong SKU, gets prompt-injected, or loops, the money is simply gone. Visa and Mastercard still have no binding agent-chargeback rule, and the ledger shows only amount, time and merchant, with no record of why the agent paid. Merchants cannot tell a legitimate agent buyer from an abusive one, and PSPs cannot price the risk.
solution: An API that wraps agent-initiated push payments in a short programmable hold (2-24h) through a licensed partner PSP's escrow or split-payment accounts, or through UPI block-and-debit mandates. Each payment carries a signed 'decision receipt': the user's mandate, a hash of the agent's tool-call trace, price-check evidence and model version. A small human adjudication desk releases or refunds by published rules. PSPs, merchants and insurers all accept the receipt as evidence. The SDK is free; money movement and adjudication are the paid layer.
why_now: Agent rails (AP2 mandates, Mastercard Verifiable Intent, MPP, x402, ACP/UCP) all solve authorization but none define fault or evidence for push rails. India ends zero-MDR UPI for large P2M payments on Oct 15, and a rail that starts charging merchants acquires card-like dispute expectations. Insurers are adding AI exclusions, so they need telemetry to price anything. The Ninth Circuit's 'the agent is the user' ruling pushes liability toward users and their intermediaries.
revenue_model: 0.2-0.4% of held volume, $0.02-0.05 per receipt at scale, and dispute-handling fees paid by whichever side loses. Later, an evidence-pack license to PSPs and insurers underwriting agent risk.
non_obvious_insight: In emerging markets most digital volume rides rails with no chargeback system, so agent error is an unhedged first-class risk there. Whoever holds the neutral, tamper-evident record of why an agent paid becomes the arbiter, and eventually the underwriter, for every party. The cards networks are structurally slow to solve this for rails they do not run.
first_30_days: Publish an open-source decision-receipt SDK for agents that pay via Pix or UPI. Recruit 10 small agent builders (WhatsApp bill-pay and shopping bots) on developer communities. Sign one licensed PSP for escrow sandbox accounts. Hand-adjudicate the first 100 disputes yourselves to learn the fault taxonomy, then price the hold as a paid tier.

title: Deorphanization Factory for AI-Nominated Enzymes
one_liner: A pooled-substrate, NGS-readout assay line that assigns function to hundreds of AI-nominated unknown enzymes per week for hundreds of dollars each.
customer: Genome-editing and enzyme-discovery companies, frontier-lab and academic agent-discovery teams, and industrial enzyme groups.
problem: Agent swarms nominate candidates far faster than anyone can characterize them. Anthropic's run went from 200,000+ reverse transcriptases to 20 candidates in 21 hours, yet the function of the resulting array-associated reverse transcriptase (ART) system is still unknown, with human validation and biochemical characterization as the bottleneck.
solution: Cell-free expression of candidates in 384-well format. Universal substrate panels of pooled, barcoded DNA and RNA oligo libraries are incubated with each enzyme. NGS reads out cutting, copying, ligating and editing, producing an automated activity 'passport' (substrate preferences, cofactors, temperature). Start with nucleic-acid-acting enzymes (nucleases, RTs, recombinases, ligases) where pooled NGS readout works, and add mass-spec panels for small-molecule enzymes later.
why_now: Anthropic's Sept 2026 ART discovery came with an explicit invitation to partner with other scientists. DNA synthesis is cheap, cell-free expression is mature, and agent discovery volumes are exploding.
revenue_model: $300-1,000 per enzyme passport, $50-250k discovery-partnership programs, and shared upside on licensed hits.
non_obvious_insight: Compute is commoditizing discovery, so the scarce step is cheap, standardized characterization. Pooled assays turn function into a read instead of a project. A passport format could become the exchange currency between agent discoverers and enzyme users.
first_30_days: Build a v0 pooled-substrate library and assay for reverse transcriptases and nucleases. Characterize 50 public candidates and publish the results. Approach 5 editing-tool companies and 3 academic agent-discovery groups with a $10k 50-enzyme pilot.

title: Care-First Reverse Mortgages With Locked Payouts
one_liner: A care-planning broker that funds long-term care from home equity and releases the money only to verified caregivers and facilities.
customer: Homeowners 70-85 with $300k+ equity and thin liquid savings, or their adult children holding a power of attorney. The channel is elder-law attorneys, geriatric care managers and hospital discharge planners.
problem: Long-term-care insurance is failing policyholders: Genworth has about $31.8B of approved premium hikes, and 2023 hikes averaged 51%. Care runs $75-115k a year, and Medicaid retrenchment is coming. The one big asset is home equity, but advisors still treat reverse mortgages as a last resort and lump sums invite fraud and sibling fights.
solution: Start with a 12-month care budget and plan. Match it to a reverse-mortgage line of credit (HECM or proprietary), through an NMLS-licensed broker or a co-brokering partner. Then open a care wallet: funds go only to vetted payees (agency, facility, or a family caregiver under a documented personal-care agreement with payroll), with a ledger for siblings and Medicaid look-back records, and multi-party approval for any other outflow.
why_now: Proprietary reverse mortgages now hold 52% share against 48% for HECM, so products are better. Seniors hold $14.92T in home equity. LTC insurance is unravelling, the 80+ cohort is exploding, and elder fraud hit $7.7B in 2025 (up 59%), which makes lump-sum liquidity risky without controls.
revenue_model: Broker origination compensation on funded loans, roughly 1-2% of loan amount, plus a $49 a month care-wallet fee. Licensing the wallet to lenders as a fraud-protection differentiator is later upside.
non_obvious_insight: The product isn't the loan; it's controlled disbursement plus a care plan. Reverse mortgages are viewed with suspicion because of how the cash gets spent, and a locked, audited payout stream fixes the exact failure mode that ruined the category's reputation.
first_30_days: Partner with a licensed reverse-mortgage broker, publish 'how to pay for care with home equity' content, and build referral relationships with 10 elder-law firms and care managers. Loans close in about 60-75 days, so first revenue lands inside six months.

title: Deadline-Proof AI Overflow and PII Shield for CPA Firms
one_liner: A browser extension that strips client SSNs, EINs and bank numbers before any AI tool sees them, and routes work to a compliant pay-as-you-go model when the firm's licensed AI hits its usage cap in the middle of a deadline.
customer: Accounting, tax and bookkeeping firms with 3 to 30 people, plus the MSPs that run their IT. All of them have written-security-program duties under the FTC Safeguards Rule.
problem: In 2026 vendors are moving to usage-based AI billing (Microsoft now uses Copilot Credits with administrator spending limits). When a firm's tool hits its cap mid-deadline, staff face three options: work stops, costs climb, or they improvise with personal consumer accounts. Uploading client statements and spreadsheets to unvetted tools breaks the Safeguards Rule's service-provider oversight requirement. Firms have no visibility into what left the building.
solution: A lightweight extension and gateway. First, it detects client PII (SSNs, EINs, account and routing numbers, dates of birth) in prompts and uploads and swaps in reversible tokens, with the mapping kept locally on the user's device. Second, it meters each seat's usage against the firm's licensed tools and, at 80% of a cap, offers an approved overflow route to a zero-retention model API billed at wholesale token cost plus a margin. Third, it writes an audit log that maps directly onto the firm's written information security program: who used what, which data classes were blocked, and which vendors were approved. Pre-purchased burst capacity is sold before each crunch (Oct 15 extension deadline, Mar 15, Apr 15).
why_now: The relevant CPA Practice Advisor article is dated Sept 28, 2026 (today). The Oct 15 extension deadline is 17 days away. Usage-based AI billing became normal this year. Firms are cutting headcount but software costs don't fall with it, so overflow spend competes with shrinking budgets.
revenue_model: $19 per seat per month for the shield and audit log, plus metered overflow at token cost +30%. Burst-capacity packs of $99 to $499 per season. MSPs and state CPA society partnerships get a channel margin of about 20%.
non_obvious_insight: The risk is not the AI model, it is the capacity cliff at the worst possible moment, which pushes careful staff into shadow tools. CPA Practice Advisor states: 'When a firm's AI tool hits its usage cap mid-deadline, staff often turn to free consumer tools', cites the FTC Safeguards Rule requirement for a written information security program and oversight of service providers, and quotes IBM's finding that high shadow-AI usage adds about $670,000 to breach costs, with 63% of breached organizations having no AI governance policy (https://www.cpapracticeadvisor.com/2026/09/28/token-limits-are-creating-a-shadow-ai-problem-for-accounting-firms/190633/). A companion piece shows why buying more seats isn't the answer: software costs stay flat when headcount falls, with contracts fixed until the notice deadline (https://www.cpapracticeadvisor.com/2026/09/03/why-client-software-costs-dont-fall-when-headcount-does-and-what-advisors-should-review/189557/).
first_30_days: Week 1: build the redaction extension for Chrome/Edge with regex plus a small detector, and a simple metering dashboard. Pitch it in accounting communities and state CPA society newsletters as a 'get through Oct 15' tool. Weeks 2 to 3: onboard 10 firms free for the extension season in exchange for testimonials and audit-log feedback. Week 4: convert to $19 per seat and sell burst packs ahead of the next crunch; approach two MSPs that serve CPA firms. Target: 8 paying firms and 1 MSP partner.

title: Konbini Pulse: Owner-Run Launch Verdict Panel
one_liner: A paid panel of convenience-store owners who report real shelf sell-through of new items in the first 48 hours after each Tuesday launch, sold to food makers who otherwise see only HQ's verdict.
customer: Small and mid-size food and beverage makers, including OEM and private-label suppliers and exclusive-item partners of the big three chains, at ¥150k-500k per brand per month. Later customers are ad agencies, trend and product-development teams, and investors who follow listed food companies.
problem: Every chain launches dozens to hundreds of new items on Tuesdays. An item's fate is effectively decided in 3-10 days, and HQ decides listing and delisting on its own data. The maker, who invested in a line, packaging and ingredients, sees only what HQ tells them. Owners see the real signal: stock-out times, leftover at closing, repeat buyers versus first-day curiosity, counter comments, and differences between office districts and residential areas. That information is never shared with the supplier. Makers cannot tell whether a delisting was fair, so they cannot negotiate.
solution: A 30-second phone routine for each owner: photograph the shelf at fixed times on days 1, 2 and 3, log leftover count at the disposal scan, and tap one of a few reasons customers gave. The panel of 40-150 stores across chains and neighborhoods is aggregated into a '48-hour verdict' delivered to the maker by Thursday: sell-through curve, sell-out time, leftover, repeat rate, and buyer profile by district type. It uses shelf observations and the owner's own counts, not HQ system exports, to reduce contractual risk. Owners are paid monthly, so the panel is a new income line that does not depend on royalty.
why_now: Ingredient and rice inflation has squeezed maker margins, so a failed launch is more expensive than before. SKU churn is accelerating. Japan's revised subcontract law, in force since January 2026, tightens buyers' duty to negotiate prices with commissioned manufacturers, so evidence has value in negotiations. Alternative-data buyers and product teams have no view into konbini shelves, because chain POS data is proprietary.
revenue_model: Subscription per brand, ¥150k-500k a month, plus ¥50k per launch report for smaller makers. Custom studies and delisting-defense reports cost ¥300k-1M. Owners receive ¥8-15k a month in cash plus a revenue share. Aggregate trend data is licensed to agencies and investors.
non_obvious_insight: Suppliers are structurally blind because the only party that counts their sales is the party that decides their fate. The owners standing at the shelf are the only independent observers, and they are invisible to the market because no one pays them. Once owners are paid to observe, the supplier's negotiating position changes. The moat is a trusted network of owners, not software. Data that comes from a shelf photo and a leftover count is less exposed to franchise confidentiality clauses than POS exports.
first_30_days: Recruit 12 stores across the three chains in Osaka through owner chat groups and the franchisee union, paying ¥10k a month each. Build a phone app that takes shelf photos on a schedule and captures counts in a few taps. Choose the next Tuesday launch wave and produce one '48-hour verdict' for five Osaka-area makers with konbini exclusives, offered at ¥50k per launch. Get legal review of the franchise contract clauses on data before scaling. Convert three makers to monthly subscriptions by day 90.

title: Appeal Kits for Musicians Wrongly Flagged as AI
one_liner: A DAW-side watcher that quietly notarizes your project history, so a wrongful 'AI' flag becomes a one-click appeal instead of a lost royalty stream.
customer: Independent producers and singer-songwriters releasing 5-50 tracks a year on TIDAL, Deezer, Spotify and Bandcamp, plus small labels and distributor support desks that have to rule on flagged tracks.
problem: Platforms now punish fully-AI tracks: TIDAL demonetizes them (Jul 15, 2026), Spotify excludes AI-persona profiles from recommendations (Aug 11), and Bandcamp banned AI music outright (Jan 14). Detectors are probabilistic, and with AI above 50% of Deezer uploads, thresholds will tighten and false positives will grow (my inference). A wrongly flagged human has no evidence and no appeal format. The free verified-artist badges do nothing for someone already flagged.
solution: A background agent for Ableton, Logic, Reaper and FL Studio (Ableton .als files are gzipped XML, so they diff cleanly) that hashes project files, stems, plugin chains and automation over time. It anchors the hashes to a public timestamp log and renders a shareable 'Session Timeline' page. One click exports an appeal packet formatted for each platform's dispute flow, with a verify link that distributors can check. Artists choose what to reveal and never upload raw sessions.
why_now: Enforcement went live in a six-month burst (Bandcamp Jan 2026, TIDAL Jul 15, Spotify Aug 11), so 'flagged as AI' now costs money and reach rather than a label. Detection is increasingly automated and at volume. Nobody has built the defendant's side of the process.
revenue_model: $9/month artist plan, $49 per notarized appeal packet for non-subscribers, $500-2,000/month label plans, and a per-verification API fee from distributors that want to clear flagged-track disputes faster.
non_obvious_insight: Nobody pays for proof-of-human in advance, because the badge is free. They pay at the moment of dispute. Sell the evidence, like a dashcam that is only valued after the crash, and not the badge.
first_30_days: Weeks 1-2: build a project-file watcher for Ableton and Reaper with a hosted timeline page. Weeks 3-4: recruit 30 producers from r/WeAreTheMusicMakers and producer Discords, and DM artists who have posted about false AI flags. Offer a free install and charge only for the first appeal packet. Pitch two distributor support leads on accepting the verify link.

title: True Pop: De-duplicated Card Scarcity Data
one_liner: A data product that uses image matching to remove crack-and-resubmit double counts from graded-card population reports, showing lenders and dealers how many physical copies actually exist.
customer: Lenders and financiers that take graded cards as collateral, high-end dealers and auction houses, investment-minded collector groups, and insurers pricing slabs.
problem: Population reports count submissions, not unique cards. A card that is cracked and resubmitted is counted twice unless the owner mails back the slip, which most do not. Yet prices, loans and low-pop premiums key off those numbers. With a roughly 12x price gap between PSA 10 and PSA 9 at the top, the incentive to resubmit is enormous, so the most valuable cards are the most double-counted.
solution: For the top ~500 cards by value, ingest public cert-lookup images and sale photos and compute surface fingerprints (print defects, edge whitening, dings) to link cert numbers that are the same physical card. Publish a True Pop and a scarcity-adjusted price index, then add cert-duplicate alerts for buyers at purchase time.
why_now: A PSA 10 Pikachu Illustrator sold for $16.5M in Feb 2026, and cards are now used as loan collateral. Vision models make surface matching cheap. The pop report is treated as truth precisely as the money grows.
revenue_model: API and subscriptions of $300-2,000/month for lenders and dealers, $9 per-card reports for collectors, and data licensing to marketplaces.
non_obvious_insight: Everyone treats the pop report as the scarcity ground truth, so scarcity is systematically mispriced in one direction, and it is worst exactly where the dollars are. The wedge is a corrected number that lenders can underwrite against.
first_30_days: Hand-verify duplicates on 200 high-value cards using public cert pages. Publish a free weekly True Pop on X and Reddit for reach. Sell 3 pilot reports at $500 to dealers or lenders and interview 5 lenders. Get legal review of scraping and terms of use first, and use only public or user-submitted data.

title: Biotech Graveyard Data Exchange
one_liner: Rescue, clean and license the wet-lab data of shutting-down biotechs, especially the failed and negative results that AI drug-discovery models are starved of, and split the proceeds with the estate.
customer: AI-drug-discovery companies, big-pharma computational groups and ML-for-bio labs that license proprietary training data (ADME/tox, assay panels, SAR series, structural data). The sellers are wind-down estates, VCs and founders, who get a revenue share instead of paying anything.
problem: After the 2022-2025 biotech funding drought, hundreds of venture-backed biotechs have shut down or been hollowed out. When the last employee leaves, years of proprietary experimental data die on unpaid cloud accounts, expired ELN and LIMS licenses and laptops. Meanwhile AI models are trained on published literature, which is survivorship-biased: negative results almost never get published. Models lack the data on what does not work, and that data is exactly what dead companies hold.
solution: A wind-down data-salvage service, done in a 60-day window between the last payroll and server deletion. Triage what data exists and what is encumbered (licensor and CRO rights, academic-license terms). Extract from ELN, LIMS, instruments and cloud buckets. Limit the first scope to non-human-subject data such as biochemical and cell assays, chemistry, DMPK and structural data, so there is no PII problem. Get IP and rights sign-off from the estate or assignee. Standardize to a common assay schema with provenance. License as curated bundles to AI-bio and pharma buyers, with revenue flowing back to the estate.
why_now: The biotech shutdown and reverse-merger wave is in full swing, with wind-down specialists and startup shutdown services now established. AI-bio companies and pharma are openly competing for proprietary data, including federated and data-for-model-access programs. The 23andMe data-in-bankruptcy episode showed how badly data is currently handled in wind-downs. Cheap LLM-assisted schema mapping now makes normalizing messy legacy assay data affordable.
revenue_model: Free or low-cost triage for the estate. Take 30-50% of licensing revenue on each bundle, plus a fixed curation fee charged to buyers. Later, sell subscription access to a growing pooled 'negative results' corpus organized by target class.
non_obvious_insight: The dataset with the most scarcity value is the one everyone considers worthless: failed programs. Sellers are motivated because the alternative is deletion, and there is no consumer-privacy problem in assay data, unlike almost every other 'data for AI' market. The moat is trust and presence at the exact moment a company dies, meaning relationships with wind-down lawyers, biotech VCs and CFO-for-hire networks, not technology.
first_30_days: Reach out to 20 biotech VC platform partners, wind-down lawyers and fractional CFOs with a one-page offer of free data triage, revenue share and zero cost to the estate. Sign 2-3 shutting-down biotechs. Pre-sell sample packs to 3-5 AI-bio buyers and get a letter of intent on price per curated dataset. Build the minimal schema-normalization pipeline on the first dataset and get legal templates for estate-to-exchange licensing. Ship the first licensed bundle within the first 2-3 months.

title: Roll Up the Layer Under Funeral Homes
one_liner: Instead of buying funeral homes, buy the removal services and wholesale crematories that independent homes depend on, and run them with AI dispatch, chain-of-custody and paperwork agents.
customer: Independent funeral homes, roughly 60% to 70% of which have no crematory of their own, plus hospice and medical-examiner contractors. Families are indirect beneficiaries.
problem: Consolidators are buying the retail funeral homes that families see, and independents are squeezed. Independents struggle to staff 24/7 first-call removals, outsource cremation to small crematories with uneven chain-of-custody, and lose days chasing physician signatures in state electronic death registration systems. Families cannot see where their loved one is.
solution: Buy regional removal companies and wholesale crematories from retiring owners. AI ops layer: a dispatch agent for 3 a.m. first calls and routing, barcode and photo chain-of-custody at every handoff with a family-facing status link (like package tracking), a paperwork agent that chases physician and ME signatures and files EDRS entries, permits and cremation authorizations, and capacity balancing across retorts. Sell independents a per-case bundle that lets them offer end-to-end service without capital or overnight staff.
why_now: Independent homes face consolidation pressure and the shift to cremation, and overnight labor is scarce. States are modernizing death-registration workflows (for example Michigan's March 2026 HB 4077 and 4078), and voice and browser agents can now do first-call dispatch and portal filing.
revenue_model: $150 to $300 per removal, $250 to $450 per wholesale cremation, and $50 to $100 per case for paperwork. A typical home with 150 cases per year yields $60k to $120k of annual revenue.
non_obvious_insight: Everyone is buying the storefront. The stickier profit pools are the invisible utilities behind thousands of small homes, and the hard parts (3 a.m. dispatch, custody proof, signature chasing) are exactly what AI operations do well. Serving independents also positions the roll-up as their ally against consolidators.
first_30_days: Ride along with one or two removal services. Offer five funeral homes a 'paperwork chaser' that monitors EDRS status and emails doctors, at about $60 per case. Then buy or partner with the removal company serving them, using seller notes. Build the family status link early and let funeral directors show it to families.

title: Servicer-Funded Nonrenewal Rescue Agent for Homeowners
angle: Pairing 1: AI agents & agent economy x Finance
one_liner: When a homeowner's policy is nonrenewed, an agent contests the machine-made underwriting flag, documents mitigation and reshops 30 carriers plus the FAIR plan, paid by the mortgage servicer that would otherwise face a coverage lapse.
customer: Mortgage servicers and credit-union lenders pay per rescued loan; homeowners get the service free; a licensed partner agency earns placement commission.
problem: Homeowner nonrenewals are at records (a record 6,200 in New Mexico, Utah highest in 2025), premiums now rival mortgage payments, and California just passed three nonrenewal and claims bills (2026-09-03). Reinsurance is softening and cat bonds are at record issuance, yet primary policyholders see none of it. Carriers increasingly rely on aerial-imagery and AI scores (roof condition, overhanging trees, tarps) that are often wrong or fixable for a few hundred dollars, and homeowners have no one to contest a machine or work 30 quote portals.
solution: On a nonrenewal or a 25%+ renewal spike (detected from escrow data), a consumer-side agent gathers the stated reason, pulls imagery evidence where the state requires disclosure, and assembles a rebuttal or cure package (photos, contractor invoices, mitigation credits). In parallel it runs quotes across carrier and FAIR-plan portals acting as the user, and a licensed partner agency binds coverage. The servicer sees coverage status in a dashboard.
why_now: Nonrenewals are at records and states are adding rules. Softening reinsurance leaves carriers room to take documented risk back. Agentic browsers acting as the user now have appellate support (Ninth Circuit, 2026-08-04). Servicers face lapse, force-placed coverage and delinquency risk as insurance stress rises.
revenue_model: $100-250 per rescued loan from the servicer, 8-15% placement commission through the licensed agency, and contractor referral fees for cure work.
non_obvious_insight: The person in pain cannot pay, but the party whose collateral and cash flow depend on continuous coverage can. The counterparty is now a machine, so the rescue has to run at machine speed and machine cost: dollars per case for an agent versus hours for a human broker is what makes a $150 servicer fee profitable.
first_30_days: Pick one state (Colorado, Utah or Oklahoma). Partner with one credit union or regional servicer and run a free pilot on about 200 borrowers with nonrenewal notices, which they see in escrow analysis. Work the first 20 cases semi-manually with a licensed agency partner, track reinstatement and placement rates and cost per case, then quote the servicer a per-rescue fee.

title: Insurer-Backed Self-Certified Permits for ADUs
one_liner: Japan-style private building confirmation: AI code review plus a licensed private reviewer plus an insurer-backed compliance warranty, so an ADU or small addition gets a certified package in about 48 hours where state law allows private providers.
customer: ADU builders, residential designers and architects, and homeowners in states with private-provider or third-party review statutes (Florida first), later cities piloting insured expedited review.
problem: Honolulu residential permits average 218 days (commercial 469). Government AI tools serve reviewers, and applicant-side tools for ADU owners, small builders and rural jurisdictions are thin. Faster review even increases filings (+34%) faster than permits issued (+5%).
solution: An applicant-side pre-clearance engine reads the plan set, runs the jurisdiction's zoning, structural and energy rules, and returns a correction list in minutes. A licensed private provider signs, and a surplus-lines policy from an MGA indemnifies owner and jurisdiction against code errors, priced from the engine's error data. Where private-provider laws exist the package is submitted directly, and elsewhere it is offered as an insured fast-track pilot.
why_now: Government pilots prove review can be automated (Honolulu review cycles down 58%, Denver's $4.6M contract). LLMs can now read plan sets. The ROAD Act funds standard blueprints. Insurers are hunting for new specialty lines, and applicants are desperate.
revenue_model: $1,500-3,000 per ADU permit package. 10-15% share of warranty premium. SaaS for designers.
non_obvious_insight: Governments will never build the applicant-side tool because of conflict of interest, but insurance can do what regulators cannot: price and carry the residual risk that a bad plan slips through. Japan has let designated private bodies issue building confirmations since the late 1990s, and permit timelines there are days, not months.
first_30_days: Partner with a Florida private-provider firm. Run 20 ADU and remodel plan sets free for three designers and compare predicted corrections to actual city comments. Pre-sell to ADU builders at $1,500 and show the accuracy data to two MGAs.

title: Escrow Shock Early Warning for Servicers
one_liner: Soft reinsurance produces homeowner nonrenewals, which produce force-placed cover and escrow shortages, which produce delinquencies on servicers' books. Predict and defuse the shock before it lands.
customer: Mid-size mortgage servicers (50k-1M loans), including non-bank and credit-union servicers with loss-mitigation and hazard-insurance teams.
problem: Homeowner insurance now rivals mortgage payments (Tacoma News Tribune, Aug 2026). Nonrenewals hit records (Utah highest in 2025, New Mexico a record 6,200, county rate spikes up to 33% in H1 2026). When coverage lapses or moves to a FAIR plan, escrow analyses jump payments by hundreds of dollars a month and delinquencies follow.
solution: Score every loan for escrow-shock risk 90 days out, using state nonrenewal patterns, filed rate changes, tax data and the servicer's own hazard-insurance tracking. Then run assisted outreach before the shortage letter goes out: re-shop with an agent network, mitigation credits, and payment-plan options. Deliver dashboards and borrower-level outcomes to loss-mitigation heads.
why_now: Record nonrenewals, California's FAIR Plan taking more new loans (beinsure, Aug 2026), a HELOC surge signaling stretched households, and the household credit stress in the brief (record auto delinquencies, K-shaped economy).
revenue_model: $75-$200 per borrower resolved, or $0.50-$1.00 per loan per year SaaS. Optional share of avoided force-placed premium.
non_obvious_insight: Servicers treat insurance as lapse-tracking compliance, not delinquency prevention. A single loss-mitigation case can cost hundreds of dollars, so even a 1% reduction in shock-driven delinquency pays for the product. Target servicers with investor and regulator pressure, since some earn money on force-placed cover.
first_30_days: Build a free escrow-shock heat map for three states from public data as a lead magnet. Cold-outreach loss-mitigation heads at 30 mid-size and credit-union servicers, and sign one pilot on about 20k loans.

title: Ceremony-as-a-Service for Direct Cremation Providers
one_liner: White-label the memorial gathering that low-cost cremation providers can't deliver, so families buy a $1.5K box of ashes plus a $3.5K send-off.
customer: Direct-cremation companies (online and storefront), hospices and community organizations. Families pay for the events.
problem: NFDA projects cremation at 63.4% in 2025, rising to 82.3% by 2045. Direct-cremation providers win on price but hand families ashes with no ceremony. Consolidators' chapels and $8K packages don't fit that customer. NFDA reports 58.3% of consumers have attended services at unconventional venues, so demand exists but no one owns the coordination.
solution: A 'Celebration Desk' embedded in the provider's checkout as 'add a gathering'. A coordinator plus software books non-funeral venues (breweries, restaurants, parks, boats, halls), catering, a celebrant, a slideshow, live-stream and RSVPs. Packages are fixed-price at $1,500, $3,500 or $7,500. It also handles scattering permits and follow-up.
why_now: Direct cremation share keeps climbing. NFDA says 61.4% of consumers are interested in green options. Consolidators are structurally pinned to a 58% cremation mix and 3%+ annual price increases and cannot copy an unbundled model. Venues have empty weekday capacity and live-streaming is now trivial.
revenue_model: Fixed package fee at 35-45% gross margin, 10-15% rev share from venues and caterers, and a referral or white-label fee of $150-$300 per booked event to the cremation provider.
non_obvious_insight: Insiders see direct cremation as the industry's price-war threat. It is really an unbundling that turned the ceremony into a separate, high-margin purchase that nobody owns. The providers who created it have no event staff, and the consolidators' chapels are the wrong shape.
first_30_days: Pick one metro. Sign one direct-cremation provider and ten venues. Coordinate the first five events by hand at about $1,800 each, offered through the provider's post-arrangement email. Photograph and price each event to build the package catalog.

title: Independent Safety Registry for Pet Medicines
angle: Pairing 2: Biotech tools/synbio/lab automation/AI drug discovery x Pets & animal health/vet shortage/pet insurance
one_liner: A neutral post-market surveillance system for veterinary drugs and biologics, built on pet-insurance claims plus owner-reported outcomes.
customer: Animal-health drugmakers and biologics developers (safety and medical-affairs teams) pay subscriptions. Pet insurers and MGAs pay for cost-effectiveness analytics. Vet groups and foundations use the public lookup.
problem: Vet adverse-event reporting is voluntary and underreported, and after the 2025 controversy over reported adverse events with anti-NGF antibody injections for canine osteoarthritis, owners and vets have no independent way to weigh safety signals. Pharma-run surveillance is not trusted. Insurers hold the only longitudinal cross-clinic data, yet are pushing 19.7% premium increases on 9% more animals without knowing which treatments reduce downstream claims. New modalities (mAbs, CGMs, long-acting insulins, oral oncology, and possibly a canine longevity drug) are arriving with no owner for outcomes data.
solution: A data trust that ingests de-identified claims from partner insurers and MGAs, optional practice-management extracts, and owner-reported outcomes gathered by a QR code at the clinic. It runs disproportionality signal detection in the style of FDA Sentinel. Outputs are (a) a safety dashboard for drug makers, (b) formulary and cost-effectiveness reports for insurers, and (c) a public 'what happened to dogs like mine' lookup for vets and owners.
why_now: Premiums rose 19.7% against 9% more animals, so insurers need loss-control insight. Big biologics and Loyal's longevity program (1,317 dogs in the STAY study, FDA acceptance of efficacy and safety sections) mean a wave of new launches. IDEXX buying CoVet shows workflow data is becoming a strategic asset, and independent players need a neutral alternative.
revenue_model: Pharma subscriptions of $60-250k per product family per year. Insurer analytics contracts of $50-150k per year. Custom post-marketing studies at $100-300k. A free public tier drives owner-reported data.
non_obvious_insight: Companion-animal medicine is the last big therapeutic area with no Sentinel-style system, and insurers are the only long-lived holders of cross-clinic data. After a public safety scare, drugmakers will pay for credibility that they cannot generate themselves, and insurers will pay for the same data to reduce claims.
first_30_days: Pitch small MGAs and startup insurers (hungry for analytics, less locked into data rules) on a free pilot in exchange for a data-sharing agreement. Build signal detection for the 10 most common drugs and biologics. Publish a public report on one hot topic, then sell two pharma safety leads a pilot subscription. Expect first revenue at month 4-6.

title: Overnight First-Call Co-op for Independent Funeral Homes
one_liner: A shared night-and-weekend answering, dispatch and chain-of-custody service so small funeral homes never lose a call at 2 a.m.
customer: Independent funeral homes, especially 1-3 director shops. NFDA counts 15,401 US funeral homes, about 75% family or privately owned. Hospice and hospital partners are the second audience.
problem: Small homes burn out staff on overnight first calls or miss them. Each service is worth several thousand dollars: SCI reports average revenue per service of $5,985. Hospitals want fast pickups, and chain-of-custody mistakes are catastrophic in an industry facing scrutiny after high-profile scandals.
solution: A shared first-call desk with trained answering, dispatch to a vetted licensed removal network, and a QR-tag custody app (ID verification, photos, timestamps) from bedside to the home's cooler. Add a hospital-facing release portal and overflow transfers later.
why_now: Consolidators keep gaining scale while independents face labor constraints. Volume is flat (SCI -1.4% in Q2 2026), so each lost call matters. Post-scandal regulatory attention raises the value of documented custody.
revenue_model: Per-dispatch fees ($175-$400 by distance), $199-$499/month retainers, and software add-ons.
non_obvious_insight: Independents fear losing the call more than losing on price, and the call is decided in the first hour. Owning that hour makes you the switching layer between hospitals and independents.
first_30_days: Pick one metro. Recruit 10 independents and 3 removal contractors. Run the phone desk yourself and charge about $250 per call. Log every call to build a service-level report.

title: Blinded Diligence Bureau for AI-Biotech Financiers
one_liner: A buyer-paid, blinded prospective testing service that tells pharma BD teams, royalty funds and lenders whether an AI drug-discovery platform's claims hold up in a neutral wet lab.
customer: Pharma BD&L and search-and-evaluation teams, corporate VCs, venture lenders, synthetic-royalty funds and crossover investors underwriting AI biotechs.
problem: AI-biotech capital is enormous ($6B+ in 2026, including Isomorphic's $2.1B and Chai's $400M). Deals are headlined in biobucks: Genentech-Earendil is $55M upfront against $1.5B+ total. Buyers still rely on vendor-supplied retrospective slides. The public competitions (Adaptyv, Anthropic x Adaptyv) test protein binding only and are public, not confidential diligence on a buyer's own targets. Small-molecule, antibody and ADMET claims have no neutral test.
solution: A custom blinded bake-off. The buyer picks 5-20 targets or properties (binding, potency, developability, ADMET). Two to four shortlisted vendors submit designs under NDA. Neutral partner labs assay them blind: an Adaptyv-style lab for binders, a CRO for ADMET. The buyer gets a ranked result, hit rate versus controls, a free open-model baseline (Boltz, BindCraft and similar) and a red-flag memo. Vendors never pay for ranking.
why_now: Frontier-lab designs hit about 27% in Adaptyv's blind test (1,320 designs, 16 targets, 354 binders), so 'does it beat free open models' is now the right question. Software-only AI shops are wobbling (Schrodinger cut staff), and mega-rounds attract generalist money that cannot judge the science. At least 12 funded biotechs sold for $1B+ this year, so acquirers need fast technical diligence. Adaptyv just raised $40M, so neutral wet-lab capacity can be rented.
revenue_model: $60-250k per blinded engagement, $150k/year retainers for funds that see 10+ platforms, and anonymized aggregate 'state of AI design' reports as a secondary product.
non_obvious_insight: 'Beats a free open-source baseline' is the question nobody prices. Buyer-paid independence, with no vendor fees, is the only credible model. Neutral labs already exist to rent, and consultancies lack lab access. Competitions such as Adaptyv's are partners and lead sources, not rivals, because they are public and binder-only.
first_30_days: Pitch 5 corporate-VC and BD teams currently evaluating platforms and sign 2 pilots at $40-60k. Rent capacity from an Adaptyv-style lab and one CRO. Design a 10-target panel with 3 anonymized vendors plus an open-model baseline. Publish the methodology to build trust.

title: Insurer-Proof Watch Service for Inherited Houses
one_liner: A subscription that keeps a parent's empty house insured during probate by producing the dated inspection log insurers require, plus leak sensors and mail and utility handling.
customer: Adult children and executors managing a deceased or institutionalized parent's home from another city ($149-$249/month), reached through probate attorneys, realtors, senior move managers and estate-sale companies.
problem: Standard homeowner policies typically stop covering vandalism, theft and most water damage after 30-60 days of vacancy. Repairs from an undetected burst pipe run $10,000-$70,000 and claims have been denied at $60,000. Dedicated vacant-home policies cost roughly 25-60% more. Probate can bar sale for 9-18 months, so the house sits empty while heirs pay taxes, insurance and utilities and rarely visit.
solution: Weekly walk-throughs by vetted local checkers (off-duty inspectors, retirees) with timestamped photo and checklist logs in the format carriers accept. Add $30 cellular leak and freeze sensors, mail and utility management, seasonal tasks, and a monthly PDF the executor can hand to the insurer and the probate court. Broker partnerships handle the vacancy endorsement, and the service later hands off to cleanout and sale referrals.
why_now: The great wealth transfer is putting millions of parents' houses into estates. Cellular leak sensors are now $30, gig labor is easy to source, and homeowners carriers are tightening on vacancy as claims costs rise. Executors are increasingly remote adult children.
revenue_model: $149-$249/month subscription for 6-12 months (average lifetime about $1,500-$2,500), plus broker commission on vacancy endorsements and referral fees on cleanout and listing.
non_obvious_insight: Loss-adjuster guidance says the documentation that preserves coverage during vacancy is 'dated inspection photos with visit logs' plus utility and contractor records, so the inspection log itself is the product, and nobody sells it to heirs (https://vectorclaimsolutions.com/vacancy-clause-property-insurance/, which also cites a $60,000 vacancy-clause denial and 50-60% premiums for dedicated vacant policies). Carrying cost and vacancy-insurance friction for heirs is described at https://www.wedgewoodhomes.com/blog/vacant-house-insurance-inherited-home. Reddit was unreachable, so this is drawn from insurance and estate-practice sources describing the recurring 'we inherited Mom's house, now what?' thread pattern in r/AgingParents and r/homeowners.
first_30_days: Choose one metro. Recruit 5 checkers at about $35 per visit and buy 20 sensors. Pitch 15 probate attorneys and senior move managers with a one-page 'keep the house insured during probate' offer at $199/month. Sign 10 customers, verify with 2 carriers or agents that the log satisfies their vacancy conditions, and use that as the sales proof.

title: Decoy Employees: Canary Tokens for People
one_liner: AI-run fake accounts-payable and help-desk staffers listed where attackers scrape, with voice agents that answer, harvest attacker infrastructure and alert the real team the moment anyone probes.
customer: Security teams at mid-market and enterprise companies in finance, healthcare and professional services, MSPs, and cyber insurers.
problem: Social-engineering crews research org charts and websites to find AP staff and help-desk numbers. Voice-deepfake defenses react only after the call, and defenders get no early warning that they are being targeted. Reports of successful voice-deepfake attacks are rising fast.
solution: Create decoy personas (an AP specialist, a help-desk line) that appear in the company's staff page, vendor portals and public contact lists, never on fake LinkedIn accounts. Each has a mailbox and a monitored voice agent that engages callers safely with no connection to real systems. Every contact triggers an alert with caller number, script, requested bank changes and voice samples, feeds the SIEM, and builds a weekly attack-tempo report for insurers.
why_now: Voice cloning and real-time voice agents make plausible fake clerks cheap. Vishing has surged and attackers automate reconnaissance, so deception is one of the few defenses that scales with attacker automation.
revenue_model: $1.5-3K per month per decoy set, MSP resale, and insurer partnerships.
non_obvious_insight: Canary tokens for files and credentials are standard, but canary employees are not. Decoys turn the attacker's reconnaissance into your telemetry, so the more the attacker automates, the more signal you get.
first_30_days: Build one persona pack with a voice agent and alerting. Deploy at 5 friendly companies with legal and HR sign-off, collect 30 days of hits as proof, and price a $1K per month pilot.

title: Managed Migrations When Models Get Retired
one_liner: We replay your agent's real traces on the replacement model, fix the regressions, and hand back a patched prompt and tool config with a pass/fail report before the deprecation date.
customer: Series A-C SaaS companies and enterprise automation teams running 1-20 production agents without a dedicated eval or ML team.
problem: Model versions are retired on schedules set by others (for example GitHub scheduled the removal of several Claude and Gemini versions in Copilot on 2026-09-01). When an agent is repointed to a newer model it keeps returning success codes while tool-call formatting, JSON adherence, refusal boundaries and token use silently change. Teams without eval infrastructure find out from customers.
solution: Fixed-fee migration sprints: capture golden traces, build assertions from tool traces, schemas and business rules, run baseline versus candidate models, tune prompts and tool descriptions, and report accuracy, latency and cost. A subscription Sunset Watch tracks about 20 providers' deprecation calendars and opens migration tickets automatically, with a self-serve replay tool later.
why_now: Retirement cadence accelerated across 2025-26, agents with multi-step tool use are more fragile than chat apps, and falling token prices tempt teams to switch models constantly.
revenue_model: $8-$25k per migration sprint and $1-3k/month for Sunset Watch.
non_obvious_insight: The customers who most need migration cannot afford an eval team, which is why Y2K, Java and Windows migrations became services businesses. Deprecation calendars are set by providers, so demand is scheduled and forecastable.
first_30_days: Publish a public deprecation calendar and migration-risk checklist. Cold-offer sprints to 30 companies visibly on soon-to-be-retired models (found via job posts and public integrations). Do 2 discounted pilots.

title: Contractor Location and Payout Attestation for Sanctions Safety
one_liner: Continuous proof that remote contractors are where they say and are paid where they claim, giving employers evidence against North Korean IT-worker sanctions exposure.
customer: Startups and mid-market engineering-heavy firms using contractors, EOR and payroll platforms, staffing firms, and cyber-insurance brokers as a channel.
problem: North Korean IT-worker schemes hit 'nearly 70' and 'over 100' US companies in cases sentenced in April and May 2026. Deepfaked interviews and rented identities pass document checks, and laptops go to US-based farms. Paying a sanctioned actor is strict liability under OFAC, so the real fear for a CFO is not a fake candidate but a sanctions violation and forfeiture.
solution: Three layers: (1) a light first-90-day attestation (IP and VPN patterns, remote-access and KVM-over-IP detection, device continuity with the interview session); (2) payout-account screening (third-party or country mismatches, many workers to one account, crypto payouts); (3) shipping-address risk scoring. Output is an evidence file counsel can hand to a regulator or insurer.
why_now: The April and May 2026 sentencings show enforcement is real. Deepfake interviews are cheap and passing. The layer above hiring (payments and audit evidence) has no product, because hiring-fraud vendors focus on faces.
revenue_model: $15-30 per contractor per month, audit packs at $2-10K, insurer and broker referral fees.
non_obvious_insight: The budget belongs to finance and legal, not HR or security, and the deliverable is evidence for regulators, not a risk score. Payout accounts are the chokepoint and are far easier to screen than faces.
first_30_days: Offer 20 startups a free payout-and-shipping exposure audit from a CSV export via VC platform teams and fractional-CFO networks. Convert to $500/month monitoring and sign one cyber-insurance broker.
